source_text: Ac ne nesciremus de quo tempore loquereris; ab Adam, quem ais unum omnes fuisse, usque ad finem, qui baptizati non sunt, damnationi et diabolo obnoxios pronuntias inveniri. In qua sententia multo te perniciosius curare niteris, quam antea vulnerasti. Nam ut removeres invidiam, quae in te ruebat, quod diceres diabolum conditorem hominum; correctus confiteris Deum conditorem, sed talium, quales ascribit Manichaeus principi tenebrarum.
pass_a_gloss: And lest we not know about which time you were speaking; from Adam, whom you say one all were, unto the end, those who have not been baptized, you pronounce found liable to condemnation and to the devil. In which sentence you strive far more perniciously to cure, than you wounded before. For that you might remove the ill-will, which was rushing upon you, that you would say the devil the founder of humans; corrected you confess God the founder, but of such, as the Manichaean ascribes to the prince of darkness.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: So that we could not miss the period you mean, you declare that from Adam, who you say was all people in one, until the end, those who have not been baptized are found liable to condemnation and subject to the devil. By this opinion you try to cure yourself far more destructively than you previously wounded yourself. For to remove the hostility rushing upon you because you called the devil humanity's Creator, you correct yourself by acknowledging God as Creator, but of the sort of people the Manichaean assigns to the prince of darkness.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
